G5429.d: from φρήν; thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while σοφός denotes practical skill or acumen; and συνετός indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative):--wise(-r).

G5382.d: from φίλος and ξένος; fond of guests, i.e. hospitable:--given to (lover of, use) hospitality.

G5457.d: from an obsolete (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; compare φαίνω, φημί); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative):--fire, light.

G5358.d: from φίλος and ἀγαθός; fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue:--love of good men.

G5072.d: neuter of a compound of τέσσαρες and μήν; a four months' space:--four months.

G5366.d: from φίλος and ἄργυρος; fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious:--covetous.

G5375.d: plural of Φίλιππος; Philippi, a place in Macedonia:--Philippi.

G5002.d: from τάσσω; arranged, i.e. appointed or stated:--set.

G5463.d: a primary verb; to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well:--farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice.

G5195.d: from ὕβρις; to exercise violence, i.e. abuse:--use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully).

G5371.d: from φιλέω; friendly; Philemon, a Christian:--Philemon.

G5166.d: from a derivative of (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); to collect the vintage:--gather.

G5103.d: of Latin origin but uncertain significance; Titus, a Christian:--Titus.

G5323.d: of Hebrew origin (פְּנוּאֵל); Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite:--Phanuel.

G5198.d: from ὑγιής; to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine):--be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some).

G5244.d: from ὑπέρ and φαίνω; appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty:--proud.

G5204.d: from the base of ὑετός; water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively:--water.

G5486.d: from χαρίζομαι; a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty:--(free) gift.

G5141.d: strengthened from a primary (to "dread", "terrify"); to "tremble" or fear:--be afraid, trembling.

G5008.d: of Chaldee origin (compare טָלֶה); the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden):--talitha.

G5223.d: from ὑπάρχω; existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth:--goods, substance.

G5029.d: as if neuter plural of ταχύς (adverbially); shortly, i.e. (figuratively) possibly:--peradventure(-haps).

G5225.d: from ὑπό and ἄρχομαι; to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb):--after, behave, live.

G5049.d: adverb from τέλειος; completely, i.e. (of hope) without wavering:--to the end.

G5085.d: from Τιβέριος; Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine:--Tiberias.

G5089.d: perhaps akin to the alternate of αἱρέομαι, and thus to σύρω; to pull off:--pluck.

G5235.d: from ὑπέρ and βάλλω; to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent):--exceeding, excel, pass.

G5337.d: apparently a primary word; "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked:--evil.

G5168.d: from a derivative of (to wear away; akin to the base of τραῦμα, τρίβος and τρώγω); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye:--eye. Compare τρύπημα.

G5108.d: (including the other inflections); from τοί and οὗτος; truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality):--like, such (an one).

G5165.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; a bowl:--dish.

G5177.d: probably for an obsolete (for which the middle voice of another alternate (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; akin to the base of τίκτω through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with εἰ), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with οὐ, extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were):--be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh…self, + special. Compare τύπτω.

G5077.d: from (ashes); to incinerate, i.e. consume:--turn to ashes.

G5106.d: from τοί and νῦν; truly now, i.e. accordingly:--then, therefore.

G5306.d: comparative from ὑπό (in the sense of behind); later:--latter.

G5142.d: a primary verb (properly, ; but perhaps strengthened from the base of τροπή through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear):--bring up, feed, nourish.

G5007.d: neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of (to bear; equivalent to φέρω); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent":--talent.

G5379.d: from φιλόνεικος; quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute:--strife.

G5406.d: from φόνος; a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which ἀνθρωποκτόνος does not necessarily imply; while σικάριος is a special term for a public bandit):--murderer.

G5302.d: from ὕστερος; to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient):--come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse.

G5474.d: neuter of a compound of χαλκός and λίβανος (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre:--fine brass.

G5059.d: of uncertain affinity; a prodigy or omen:--wonder.

G5334.d: from φημί (not the same as "phase", which is from φαίνω); a saying, i.e. report:--tidings.

G5020.d: from (the deepest abyss of Hades); to incarcerate in eternal torment:--cast down to hell.

G5498.d: neuter of a compound of χείρ and γράφω; something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)):--handwriting.

G5189.d: from a derivative of τύφω; stormy (as if smoky):--tempestuous.

G5493.d: from the base of χειμών and ῥέω; a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent:--brook.

G5339.d: of uncertain affinity; to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently:--forbear, spare.

G5455.d: from φωνή; to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation:--call (for), crow, cry.

G5016.d: feminine from ταράσσω; disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition:--trouble(-ing).

G5013.d: from ταπεινός; to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart):--abase, bring low, humble (self).

G5174.d: from (a Trojan); the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor:--Troas.

G5398.d: from φόβος; frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable:--fearful, terrible.

G5489.d: from the same as χάραξ; a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over):--paper.

G5212.d: from ὑμεῖς; yours, i.e. pertaining to you:--your (own).

G5466.d: probably of Hebrew or (כַּשְׂדִּי); a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates:--Chaldæan.

G5274.d: from ὑπό and λαμβάνω; to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume):--answer, receive, suppose.

G5396.d: from φλύαρος; to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously:--prate against.

G5136.d: from τράχηλος; to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare):--opened.

G5403.d: from φοῖνιξ; palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine:--Phenice, Phenicia.

G5309.d: from a compound of ὑψηλός and φρήν; to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant:--be highminded.

G5079.d: from τέχνη; an artisan; figuratively, a founder (Creator):--builder, craftsman.

G5000.d: of Chaldee origin (compare צְבִיָּה); the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female:--Tabitha.

G5328.d: of foreign origin (פַּרְעֹה); Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king:--Pharaoh.

G5187.d: from a derivative of τύφω; to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit:--high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud.

G5202.d: from a compound of ὕδωρ and a derivative of πίνω; to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages:--drink water.

G5384.d: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.):--friend.

G5285.d: from ὑπό and πνέω; to breathe gently, i.e. breeze:--blow softly.

G5138.d: perhaps strengthened from the base of ῥήγνυμι (as if jagged by rents); uneven, rocky (reefy):--rock, rough.

G5418.d: from φράσσω; a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively):--hedge (+ round about), partition.

G5326.d: from φαντάζω; (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre:--spirit.

G5449.d: from φύω; growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage:--(man-)kind, nature(-al).

G5206.d: from a presumed compound of υἱός and a derivative of τίθημι; the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God):--adoption (of children, of sons).

G5335.d: prolongation from the same as φημί; to assert:--affirm, profess, say.

G5431.d: from a derivative of φρήν; to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious:--be careful.

G5490.d: from a form of an obsolete primary (to "gape" or "yawn"); a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval):--gulf.

G5279.d: from ὑπό and μιμνήσκω; to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory:--put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance.

G5115.d: from the base of τίκτω; a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric):--bow.

G5433.d: akin to βρύω, βρύχω; to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult:--rage.

G5036.d: of uncertain affinity; fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready:--swift.

G5238.d: from ὑπέρ and the neuter plural of ἐκεῖνος; above those parts, i.e. still farther:--beyond.

G5445.d: from a prolonged form of (to mix a liquid with a solid; perhaps akin to φύω through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough:--lump.

G5255.d: from ὑπακούω; attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive:--obedient.

G5003.d: from ταλαίπωρος; to be wretched, i.e. realize one's own misery:--be afflicted.

G5362.d: from φίλος and ἀνήρ; fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife:--love their husbands.

G5132.d: probably contracted from τέσσαρες and πεζῇ; a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest):--bank, meat, table.

G5071.d: plural from τέσσαρες and ἑκατόν; four hundred:--four hundred.

G5088.d: a strengthened form of a primary (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively:--bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail.

G5350.d: probably akin to φέγγος and thus to φημί; to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim:--speak.

G5100.d: an enclitic indefinite pronoun; some or any person or object:--a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever).

G5146.d: from τρεῖς and βέλος; properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop):--brier, thistle.

G5336.d: from (to eat); a crib (for fodder):--manager, stall.

G5154.d: ordinal from τρεῖς; third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly:--third(-ly).

G5034.d: from the same as ταχύς; a brief space (of time), i.e. (with ἐν prefixed) in haste:--+ quickly, + shortly, + speedily.
